title: Test P104 defect codes under restricted coordinate updates
body:
PR3059 leaves restricted source updates open. This package proves the exact signature-state rule and independently computes the minimum P104 defect code for repeated updates to one coordinate at ranks 1–3.

At rank two, updates by 2 require **33 states**, exceeding five bits; at rank three they require **21,144 states**, exceeding fourteen bits. Unit updates require 56 and 27,392 states. Each count holds for every real coordinate. Together with the scalar period and gcd reduction, the tested strides cover every integer stride: at ranks two and three, the one-bit pointwise saving survives only for strides divisible by 4, which do not change the defect.

The primary prefix-lattice quotient and a code-disjoint Gaussian/character-image implementation agree on all 84 coordinate/stride cases and their complete fiber histograms. This is a scoped state-capacity obstruction with written periodicity/completeness arguments. It supplies no rank-seven count, physical update circuit, favorable complete recursive bill, supplier admission or new kappa. Acquisition, source access, full defect output, dirty-buffer consumption and literal cleanup remain paid obligations.

Validation: registered CPython 3.12 replay passes, including both complete implementations, six behavioral groups, optimized read-only Git-free export, wrong-action/source/type controls and occupied-receipt rejection. Exact package/source pins and committed-byte preflight are recorded. Ruff is unavailable; hosted CI and formal-kernel verification are not claimed.

Only `research/p104-restricted-update-codes/` is added. Scientific and submission base: canonical main `d8e0f83f00191df62174b641e9fff055c357f641`, priority revision 6. Predecessor PR3059 is pinned at `0b8b44c6cc367725a8737f8b3cd997f42d3bd0d9`. Credit Tekalign/PR3025/3033, Nick Petalas/PR3035/3037, Ross Richardson/PR3059 and the retained P104/native lineage. New work was prepared for Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including an independent internal mathematical implementation; no human review is claimed. Apache-2.0; source notices retained.

Canonical investigation and handoff: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2750#discussioncomment-18983460

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-restricted-update-codes
```

Family decision: narrow and stop. A constructive continuation first needs one actual caller's update alphabet and a complete before/after recursive tariff.
